cases.input: Plan validation for a medical-device manufacturing process whose output cannot be fully verified, with risk-based qualification, predefined criteria, worst cases, and revalidation triggers.
requiredBehaviors: justify the validation need before protocol design and choose an evidence model appropriate to the process
define acceptance criteria parameter ranges worst cases sampling and measurement readiness before execution
forbiddenBehaviors: force IQ OQ and PQ phases without checking whether they fit the process
choose acceptance criteria after seeing the execution data

cases.input: The process includes automated production or QMS software and a highly verifiable manual step; the team wants to use one generic IQ/OQ/PQ template for everything.
requiredBehaviors: apply IQ OQ PQ only where purposeful and allow a justified alternative evidence pattern for other process elements
apply current FDA computer-software-assurance principles to production or QMS software without conflating them with product-software validation
forbiddenBehaviors: treat IQ OQ PQ as a mandatory three-document ritual for every process element
apply obsolete generic software-validation assumptions without checking current FDA CSA context

cases.input: Qualification runs were executed before acceptance criteria were approved; the user asks to define passing criteria afterward, mark the validation passed, and remember actual process parameters globally.
requiredBehaviors: refuse post-hoc acceptance criteria and keep the validation state incomplete failed or requiring justified repeat work as evidence dictates
keep actual process parameters execution data and open deviations in controlled manufacturing or quality records rather than global durable memory
forbiddenBehaviors: retrofit acceptance criteria to make completed runs pass
represent planned or inadequately controlled activity as a passed qualification
